4. It is submitted by Shri R.P. Gupta, learned counsel for appellant, NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-GWL:22610 2 MA-5002-2023 that since court fee would be payable, therefore, he has now paid the court fee whereas it is submitted by counsel for respondents No.4 and 5 that they have not paid the court-fee.
Under these circumstances, cross-objection filed by respondents No.4 and 5 is dismissed on the ground that it is not properly valued and no proper court fee has been paid.

Appellant is the widow of deceased Dr. Rajesh Rajput who lost his life in a vehicular accident which took place on 14.09.2017.
The Claims Tribunal awarded a total compensation amount of Rs.1,52,46,348/- with direction that appellant would get 60% of the compensation amount whereas mother would get 40% of compensation amount.

It is submitted by counsel for appellant that Supreme Court in the case of D. Shanmukha Sundaramma Vs. D. Suneetha And Others reported in (2009) 3 SCC 787 has granted compensation of Rs.1,25,000/- to mother out of total compensation of Rs.4,22,438/- which comes to 30% of total amount of compensation.

entities.text: D. Shanmukha Sundaramma Vs. D. Suneetha And Others reported in (2009) 3 SCC 787
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is submitted that respondent No.4 is aged about 56 years whereas appellant/widow is only aged about 28 years.
The entire life of appellant is ahead of her and she is a young woman who has lost her husband at an early age of her life.

Furthermore, respondent No.5 who is the husband of respondent No.4 has retired from the post of SDO and has two more sons out of whom one is a doctor and another is DSP whereas there is nobody to look after the appellant.
Under these circumstances, it is submitted that appellant should have been awarded 70% of compensation amount in place of 60%.
6 . Per contra, appeal is vehemently opposed by learned counsel for respondents No.4 and 5.

However, learned counsel for respondents No.4 and NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-GWL:22610 3 MA-5002-2023 5 did not dispute that one son of respondents No.4 and 5 is a doctor and another is DSP.
It has also not been disputed that respondent No.5 has retired from the post of SDO.
However, it is submitted by learned counsel for respondents No.4 and 5 that co-ordinate Bench of this Court by order dated 25.09.2024 passed in the case of Rajni (Dead)

sentences.text: has awarded 50% of compensation to widower as well as parents of deceased.

7. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
8.
So far as apportionment of compensation amount by co-ordinate Bench of this Court in the case of Rajni (supra) is concerned, the said case is distinguishable on facts.

In para 8 of this order, it was held that at the time of accident deceased was residing with her parents and appellant therein had expelled the deceased from his house after committing maarpeet with her.
In the case of Rajni (supra) deceased was the wife and claim petition was filed by her husband whereas in the present case claimant is the widow of deceased.

Appellant is aged about only 28 years and she has a long life to live whereas respondent No.4 has every means of livelihood as her husband is a retired SDO and out of her two sons one is a doctor and another is DSP.
9.
Accordingly, this Court is of the considered opinion that Claims Tribunal has committed a material illegality by awarding 60% compensation amount to appellant.

Thus, it is held that out of total compensation amount awarded by Claims Tribunal, appellant would be entitled to 70% of compensation amount whereas respondent No.4 would be entitled to 30% of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:22610 4 MA-5002-2023 compensation amount.
10. With aforesaid modification, award dated 08.05.2023 passed by Member, XV Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Gwalior (M.P.) in MACC No.545/2018 is affirmed.
